subject: Transparency update: priorities, role consolidation & QBR prep
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rebecca (Delta) <rebecca@delta-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transparency update: priorities, role consolidation & QBR prep

Team —

As we finalize QBR materials I want to surface a short, transparent note for the group and ask for quick alignment before I share broadly next week. High level:

- Why: We need clearer ownership on ingestion, serving, and ops to meet the latency and cost OKRs.
- What: A modest role consolidation across two product squads (embedding-platform + runtime) to reduce hand-offs and speed decision loops. No org-wide layoffs; this is about refocusing capabilities and reporting lines.
- Timing: Proposed to publish the announcement the Monday before QBR (May 10) and include a detailed FAQ doc.

Attached are a one-pager rationale and the draft QBR slide set. Rebecca from Delta added a short external perspective on comms tone (cc'd).

Asks:
1) Marcus — can you confirm the proposed reporting changes on slide 6 are operationally feasible?
2) Grace — please flag any CS escalations or accounts we should pre-brief before posting.
3) Laura — can you review the external-facing paragraph (bottom of the one-pager) for tone?

Please reply with comments by EOD Wednesday (May 5). I plan to lock the message and FAQ Wednesday night.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: role_consolidation_rationale.pdf (pdf, 320KB); org_priorities_q2.pptx (pptx, 4.1MB); QBR_talking_points_v1.docx (docx, 45KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rebecca (Delta) <rebecca@delta-consulting.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transparency update: priorities, role consolidation & QBR prep

Irene — thanks for the clear framing. Quick operational notes after reviewing slide 6 and the org matrix:

- Feasible: moving the runtime infra lead under embedding-platform would reduce two coordination hops (ingest -> runtime -> model-serving). We can do this with current headcount.
- Risk: short-term pairing friction between teams during handover windows (2–3 weeks). Recommend a 4-week overlap plan with documented runbooks and a dedicated rotation scheduler.
- Ask: add a brief line in the FAQ that explains the overlap plan and where to find runbooks.

Small edits on slide 6 suggested inline (I attached a redline export).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks for pushing this. Two quick items from CS/Customer ops:

- Pre-brief list: Acme Corp (high-touch), NovaRetail, and two pilot partners in EU. Acme should get a senior-level heads-up (Laura + Irene) 48 hours before the public announcement.
- Escalation playbook: we should include a named contact for each affected account and a short FAQ line that says "how we will route incidents during the transition."

On the comms tone: I like the emphasis on "no layoffs" but would soften the phrase "role consolidation" in external copy; clients sometimes read consolidation as cost-cutting. Suggest "focused role alignment" externally.

I'll add account names to the FAQ doc and drop a CS-specific slide for QBR.

— Grace

Thanks — useful thread. A couple of redlines/asks from comms and exec alignment perspective:

1) External wording: change "role consolidation" -> "role realignment" and add one sentence about investments in hiring to reinforce this is capability-first.
2) Add a short executive Q&A (3 bullets) explaining how we will measure success (latency p95, token cost per 1M, and deployment cadence).
3) Please add a one-line leader note for the May 12 all-hands linking to the FAQ and the drop-in office hours.

I'm ok with publishing May 10 once the FAQ has the pre-brief list and the overlap/runbook line Marcus suggested. Rebecca — if you see any tone issues from an external comms point of view, flag them and I'll fold into the final.

Laura Bennett
Chief of Staff | Redwood Inference

Irene/Team — thanks for sharing the draft. From an external comms lens: a few small edits that reduce anxiety without hiding the change:

- Phrase suggestion: use "role realignment" (as Laura suggested) and add a single sentence about "no changes to current SLAs or support contacts for 30 days."
- FAQ: include an explicit line that describes who to contact if an account experiences degraded latency during the transition and promise weekly status updates for affected customers.
- Tone: keep the leadership voice human and candid — a one-paragraph quote from you will land well.

Happy to help edit the final announcement.

Rebecca
Delta Consulting (external advisor)
